summary: Bahrain admits GCC citizens freely, and offers visas on arrival and eVisas to a broad list of nationalities including the EU, US, UK, China, Japan, Brazil and Mexico; everyone else needs a visit visa arranged through a sponsor in Bahrain via the NPRA before travel, unless they hold a valid UAE, UK, US, Saudi or Schengen visa or a US Green Card, which opens the eVisa and the visa on arrival to them (except Iranian, Kosovan and North Korean passport holders, for whom the eVisa portal lists no visa).

conditionalWaivers.text: Residents of other GCC states, whatever their nationality, can apply online from outside Bahrain for a two-week single-entry eVisa (BHD 5 application plus BHD 5 issuance fee), attaching their GCC residence permit with a return visa valid for at least 3 months; issuance takes one working day.

source.name: Nationality, Passports & Residence Affairs (NPRA) — Two-Week Single Entry Electronic Visa (GCC Residents)

conditionalWaivers.text: Holders of a valid visit visa for the UAE, the UK, the USA or Saudi Arabia (not a Hajj or Umrah visa), a Schengen visa or a US Green Card can get the two-week visa on arrival (BHD 5) or apply online for the eVisa, even where their nationality otherwise needs a sponsored visa.

source.name: Bahrain eVisa (NPRA) — Visa Selection Criteria: eligibility result for each nationality and the 'See Conditions' page of each visa offered

fee.notes: BHD 5 application fee (non-refundable) plus BHD 5 visa issuance fee; an extension of 14 days costs BHD 25 and is applied for at an NPRA service centre. Longer and multiple-entry eVisas are priced separately.

source.name: Nationality, Passports & Residence Affairs (NPRA) — Two Weeks Single Entry Electronic Visa

source.name: Bahrain NPRA eVisa portal — Conditions for Visit Visa - 2 Weeks Single Entry (VB-01): Required Documents

fee.notes: Paid to the passport officer on arrival for the 2-week single-entry visa, per the conditions NPRA's eVisa portal shows for each eligible nationality.

source.name: Bahrain eVisa (NPRA) — visa eligibility check: conditions for the 2-week visa on arrival

fee.notes: BHD 5 application fee (non-refundable), BHD 5 approval fee and BHD 30 issuance fee, as listed by NPRA for general visit visas applied for by a guarantor.

source.name: NPRA Bahrain — General visit visas (guarantor): processing time, documents and fees

passportValidity.text: NPRA asks eVisa applicants for a passport valid for more than 6 months, and the UK Foreign Office says your passport must have an expiry date at least 6 months after the date you arrive in Bahrain.

source.name: Nationality, Passports & Residence Affairs (NPRA) — Two Weeks Single Entry Electronic Visa

vaccinations.name: Yellow fever
vaccinations.text: WHO lists Bahrain as requiring a yellow fever vaccination certificate from travellers aged 9 months or over who arrive from a country with risk of yellow fever transmission or transited more than 12 hours through an airport there.

source.name: WHO — International Travel and Health: country list of vaccination requirements (2022, revised 2023)

travelInsurance.text: No official source we could read states a travel-insurance requirement for entry to Bahrain. Canada's travel advice tells travellers to get insurance that covers medical evacuation and hospital stays.

source.name: Government of Canada — Travel advice and advisories: Bahrain

onwardTicket.text: eVisa applicants must attach proof of a return air ticket and a hotel reservation or an address in Bahrain, and travellers taking the 2-week visa on arrival must show a confirmed return air ticket, per NPRA. The FCDO notes you may be asked for evidence of onward or return travel when you apply.

source.name: NPRA Bahrain — Two-week single-entry eVisa: required documents and fees

alsoStatedOn.name: UK Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office — Bahrain travel advice: entry requirements
Bahrain eVisa (NPRA) — conditions for the 2-week visa on arrival

proofOfFunds.text: NPRA's two-week eVisa page asks for a bank statement for the past 3 months showing a regular income of at least USD 1,000; the eVisa portal's own conditions list a 3-month statement with an ending balance of at least USD 1,000 for some nationalities but not for others (US citizens, for example). On a visa on arrival the passport officer may ask you to prove you can support yourself, with no amount set.

source.name: NPRA Bahrain — Two-week single-entry eVisa: required documents and fees

currencyLimits.text: The US State Department gives Bahrain's currency restriction on entry as USD 10,000, without saying whether that is a declaration threshold or a limit. No Bahraini source we could read states the rule.

source.name: U.S. Department of State — Bahrain country information

notes: The UK FCDO says illegal drugs are strictly forbidden, even in residual amounts, and that you may need prior agreement from the authorities to bring prescription drugs into Bahrain; it advises carrying a doctor's note and checking with a Bahraini embassy before you travel.

safety.text: The FCDO reports strikes and retaliatory attacks by Iran in Bahrain, among other places in the region, since 8 July 2026, and warns of possible flight cancellations and periodic airspace closures. It says crime is low in most areas, that demonstrations take place and large ones should be avoided, and that filming or photographing security and military sites is prohibited.

source.name: UK Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office — Bahrain travel advice

tips.text: The UK FCDO says alcohol is legal in Bahrain, but drunken public behaviour is against the law and can lead to a fine, prison or deportation. It says drivers found with any alcohol in their system may get a fine, a travel ban and a possible prison sentence.

During Ramadan the UK FCDO advises not eating, drinking, smoking or chewing gum in public in the daytime, including in your car, and says hotels and restaurants serving food in fasting hours may separate you from Muslim guests, for example with screens.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Bahrain?
faq.answer: GCC citizens enter freely with a national ID. A broad list of nationalities — including the EU, UK, US, Canada, Australia, China, Japan, Brazil and Mexico — can get a visa on arrival or apply online for an eVisa. Nationalities outside those lists need a visit visa arranged through a sponsor in Bahrain via the NPRA before travel. Holders of a valid visit visa for the UAE, UK, US or Saudi Arabia, a Schengen visa or a US Green Card can use the eVisa or the visa on arrival, except Iranian, Kosovan and North Korean passport holders, for whom the eVisa portal lists no visa.

faq.question: Should I get the Bahrain eVisa or a visa on arrival?
faq.answer: If you are eligible for both, the visa on arrival needs no application in advance: it is issued at any entry point to Bahrain, and you need a confirmed return air ticket. The eVisa (evisa.gov.bh) is applied for before travel and NPRA also offers longer and multiple-entry eVisas; some nationalities are eligible only for the eVisa.

faq.question: I live in Saudi Arabia / the UAE — can I get a visa on arrival?
faq.answer: NPRA offers residents of GCC states, whatever their nationality, a two-week single-entry eVisa applied for online from outside Bahrain, with the GCC residence permit attached and a return visa valid for at least 3 months; issuance takes one working day.

faq.question: Can Israeli citizens visit Bahrain?
faq.answer: Israeli passport holders can apply online for the Bahrain eVisa on evisa.gov.bh before travel; accommodation details and a return ticket are required.

faq.question: Can I extend my stay in Bahrain?
faq.answer: NPRA says the two-week eVisa can be extended by 14 days for BHD 25 at an NPRA service centre, and that guarantor-sponsored visit visas can be extended (BHD 30, one working day).
